history.dynasty: ISKCON (modern, 20th century); founded under Srila Bhaktisvarupa Damodara Swami
history.summary: The ISKCON Temple of Imphal, officially the Sri Sri Radha Krishnachandra Temple, stands on Airport Road at Sangaiprou/Ghari in Imphal West district, on the banks of the Imphal river. Srila Prabhupada, aware of Manipur's rich Gaudiya Vaishnava heritage, desired to revitalize Vaishnava culture there and to visit Manipur, but ill health and the difficulty of obtaining inner-line permits for foreign devotees prevented it. In 1977, to fulfil Prabhupada's desire, Srila Bhaktisvarupa Damodara Swami opened an ISKCON temple in Imphal, now known as the Manimandir or 'Jewelled Temple'. At the deity installation, 108 Brahmins chanted the entire 18,000 verses of Srimad-Bhagavatam. The elegant white-coated brick structure (white cement over brick, resembling marble) has a distinctive dome whose paintings portray the pastimes of Lord Krishna; the sankirtan hall features carved wood and natural lighting, and the temple walls and roof carry carvings depicting the whole life of Krishna. The temple propagates Bhagavad-Gita teachings, congregational kirtan and Bhakti yoga in North-East India.

name: ISKCON Temple Imphal
town_description: Imphal is the capital of Manipur in the north-east of India, the historical seat of the Meitei kings. The ISKCON Temple lies at Sangaiprou/Ghari on Airport Road, in Imphal West district on the banks of the Imphal river - a few kilometres south-west of the city centre and close to the airport. It is a major Gaudiya Vaishnava spiritual centre of North-East India.

travel.airport: Imphal International Airport is very close - the temple sits on Airport Road at Sangaiprou/Ghari (verify exact distance, roughly 5 km).
travel.railway: Nearest railhead Dimapur, Nagaland, about 215 km away, with regular bus services to Imphal (verify).
travel.road: On Airport Road at Sangaiprou/Ghari in Imphal West district; easily reached by taxi/auto from Imphal city centre. Parking is available near the temple premises (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather (verify). Janmashtami is the most vibrant time, drawing very large crowds; Ratha Yatra and Gaura Purnima are the other major celebrations.
visitor_information.opening_hours: CONFLICT IN SOURCES (verify on site): the ISKCON centres listing shows 4:00 AM - 7:30 PM daily; one travel guide lists 4:30 AM-1:00 PM and 4:00-8:00 PM with morning and evening aarti/bhajan programs. Non-stop Hare Krishna kirtan through the day.
